To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we introduce a method to automatically adapt the contributions of different tasks to the agent’s learning process, 2) our method learns a single trained policy that can master multiple sequential decision tasks, and 3) our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on two challenging multi-task reinforcement learning domains.
(1) we propose a method that learns to play all Atari 57 games, and (2) we demonstrate that a single agent can surpass human-level performance on a set tasks.
we have shown that it is possible to learn multiple tasks in a single deep reinforcement learning agent, and we have proposed a method for doing this.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning multiple sequential decision tasks at once.
the problem of learning a set of tasks in parallel, and how to balance the contribution of the individual tasks to the learning dynamics in order to achieve good performance on all tasks.
the problem of learning general agents capable of solving a large variety of sequential decision tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a new algorithm for deep multi-task reinforcement learning that outperforms the state of the art on two different domains.
we propose a novel approach for deep multi-task reinforcement learning that outperforms previous approaches in a variety of domains.

our approach is the first one that is able to solve a large number of different Atari games with a single trained agent and that it outperforms the state of the art on both the Atari and DeepMind Lab benchmark.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a multi-task learning algorithm which is capable of learning a single policy that solves multiple sequential decision tasks.
we have developed a new algorithm for multi-task reinforcement learning that is both general and scalable to a very large number of tasks.
the PopArt approach can learn to master multiple tasks at once.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multi-task deep reinforcement learning can be made more robust to the saliency of the tasks in the set, by adapting the learning dynamics to the needs of all the tasks simultaneously.
it is possible to train agents that are capable of learning multiple sequential decision tasks at once, without the need for a separate agent per task.
a multi-task agent that is trained to solve multiple tasks at the same time, can outperform a collection of agents trained on the same tasks individually.
